briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Tensions in the Strait of Hormuz have escalated significantly with Iran attacking a Singapore-flagged cargo vessel with a drone and asserting control over maritime navigation routes. Concurrently, southern Lebanon remains an active flashpoint as Israeli forces killed multiple Hezbollah operatives while four IDF soldiers were injured in separate clashes, ahead of an anticipated framework agreement between Israel and Lebanon.

IRAN
Iran attacked a Singapore-flagged cargo vessel with a drone in the Strait of Hormuz, causing damage but no casualties, following warnings for ships to use Iran-approved routes. US President Trump described this as a "stupid violation of the ceasefire agreement" and claimed the US intercepted three other drones. Iran's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned a joint US-GCC statement, calling it "meddlesome, irresponsible, and provocative," and reiterated that national security is non-negotiable, rejecting claims against its nuclear program. Iran also issued a stern warning against "dangerous" Israeli military aircraft in neighboring airspaces, stating it reserves the right to respond if the US cannot contain Israel. Separately, Press TV reported the establishment of a communication line between Iran and the US in the Strait of Hormuz through mediators, while Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman seemed to deny a direct communication line, emphasizing that passage through Hormuz must be via routes announced by Iran. Economically, the head of the Central Bank stated $3.7 billion was supplied for essential goods and medicine, refuting US claims of supply issues. Iran is exploring charging fees for services in the Strait of Hormuz, potentially generating $40 billion annually.

ISRAEL
Israeli forces conducted multiple operations in southern Lebanon, killing seven Hezbollah operatives transporting weapons near Manzala and another six operatives in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah and the Ali Taher ridge who posed a threat to troops. Artillery and airstrikes targeted Hezbollah sites in the Beit Yahoun area after an incident. Four IDF soldiers, including two officers, were injured (one moderately, three lightly) when a Hezbollah gunman threw a grenade at them in Beit Yahoun. The IDF also dropped leaflets over Mansouri, southern Lebanon, warning residents to evacuate. Over the past week, the IDF reported more than 10 eliminations in Gaza and 6 strikes in southern Lebanon. Politically, Defense Minister Israel Katz issued a warning in Persian to Iran, stating that an attack on Israel would be its "biggest mistake" and nothing would stop Israel. Prime Minister Netanyahu reiterated that soldiers respond to immediate threats and are not restricted. Israel is expected to sign a framework agreement with Lebanon today. Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar plans to propose official recognition of the Armenian genocide to the government, a move that could heighten tensions with Turkey.

GAZA & WEST BANK
IDF operations in Gaza during the week resulted in over 10 eliminations. In the occupied West Bank, Israeli settlers reportedly set fire to Palestinian farmlands in the village of Barqa. Hamas announced that consultations are ongoing for the full implementation of a ceasefire, with a delegation expected to visit Cairo soon to respond to new proposals.

LEBANON
Hezbollah operations included a gunman throwing a grenade at Israeli troops in Beit Yahoun, injuring four IDF soldiers (one moderately, three lightly). Hezbollah operatives were observed transporting weapons near Manzala and others were identified in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah and the Ali Taher ridge. Israeli forces conducted multiple strikes, killing seven Hezbollah operatives in Manzala and six more in the Zawtar al-Sharqiyah and Ali Taher ridge areas. Artillery and airstrikes also targeted Hezbollah sites in Beit Yahoun. IDF drones dropped leaflets over Mansouri, warning residents of a "danger zone" and advising them to stay away. Hezbollah Secretary-General Sheikh Naim Qassem stated that Israel must withdraw "humiliated, defeated" from every inch of Lebanese territory. Italy and France announced a new coalition to support Lebanon after the UNIFIL mandate expires at year-end, signaling plans for a potential international conference. Israeli and Lebanese officials are reportedly set to announce a framework agreement today.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The Iraqi Ministry of Defense reported an explosion at an Al-Hashd Al-Shaabi ammunition depot in Diyala province. The central command of the Iranian armed forces, Khatam al-Anbiya, issued a warning regarding the "dangerous" presence and movements of Israeli military aircraft in the airspace of neighboring countries towards Iran. US President Trump quietly renewed an order solidifying US control over Iraqi oil revenues, directing them to a New York Federal Reserve Bank account.

GULF STATES
The US Navy's Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain, along with satellite communication facilities, warehouses, and other buildings, sustained significant damage from Iranian missile and drone attacks between late February and June, with reconstruction costs estimated at $400 million. This damage is prompting the Pentagon to reconsider its military force deployment in the region, potentially reducing presence in Kuwait and Saudi Arabia and transferring some capabilities to Israel. The UAE issued missile alerts, which were later confirmed to be false alarms caused by a technical malfunction. The UAE Foreign Minister urged his Iranian counterpart to ensure full compliance with the US-Iran interim agreement, emphasizing the protection of maritime corridors and freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. In a joint statement with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Manama, GCC foreign ministers stressed the need to address Iran's ballistic missile program, drone capabilities, and proxy support for lasting peace. Oman has informed European officials that ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz may be required to pay fees for services like navigation assistance and pollution control, a move that Iran suggests could generate significant revenue.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  Iran attacked a Singapore-flagged cargo vessel in the Strait of Hormuz with a drone, causing damage but no casualties, an act US President Trump labeled a "stupid violation of the ceasefire."
2.  Iran explicitly asserted its control over the Strait of Hormuz, declaring it Iranian territory and mandating transit only through approved routes, threatening consequences for non-compliance, and raising the prospect of charging transit fees.
3.  Israeli forces killed seven Hezbollah operatives near Manzala and six additional Hezbollah operatives in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah and Ali Taher ridge in southern Lebanon during offensive operations.
4.  Four IDF soldiers, including two officers, were injured in an encounter with a Hezbollah gunman in Beit Yahoun, southern Lebanon, following a grenade attack.
5.  The US Navy's Fifth Fleet headquarters and over 20 other US military facilities across the Middle East, particularly in Bahrain, sustained extensive damage from Iranian missile and drone attacks, leading to a Pentagon review of regional force posture.
6.  The death toll from two devastating earthquakes in Venezuela escalated dramatically to 589 fatalities and 2,980 injured, with over 50,000 reportedly missing.
7.  Israeli and Lebanese officials are expected to announce a framework agreement today following negotiations in Washington, addressing security arrangements in southern Lebanon.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are high, particularly in the Strait of Hormuz due to Iran's direct attack on shipping and its assertive stance on controlling navigation, which directly challenges international norms and US demands for free passage. Southern Lebanon remains a critical flashpoint, with ongoing IDF-Hezbollah clashes and Israeli warnings of continued military action, increasing the potential for broader conflict. The vulnerability of US bases in the Gulf, highlighted by significant damage in Bahrain from Iranian attacks, may lead to a reallocation of US forces, potentially shifting capabilities closer to Israel. Iran has declared a "red line" requiring full Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon as a condition for any final deal with the US, and has warned against Israeli military aircraft in neighboring countries. Israel, in turn, has issued strong threats against any Iranian attack.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US posture is one of denunciation of Iranian actions in Hormuz while pursuing a diplomatic track, as evidenced by Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit to Gulf states and the establishment of a US-Iran communication line in Hormuz. Gulf states, particularly the UAE and members of the GCC, called for Iran to comply with the US-Iran agreement and counter its destabilizing activities, though Oman is considering charging transit fees in Hormuz. European nations like Italy and France are forming a coalition to support Lebanon post-UNIFIL, with Italy's PM Meloni emphasizing her country's non-combat role in the Iran conflict. Russia has reportedly shot down 660 Ukrainian drones, is returning nuclear specialists to Bushehr, and exchanged 160 POWs with Ukraine via UAE mediation. Canada is considering reopening embassies in Iran and Venezuela. Japan pledged $15 million in aid to Iran, Lebanon, and the West Bank. The UN's International Maritime Organization temporarily suspended escort operations in Hormuz following the recent attack.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
There are notable contradictions regarding the US-Iran communication line in the Strait of Hormuz; Press TV and US officials affirm its establishment, albeit through mediators, while a high-ranking Iranian official directly denied a direct line with the US concerning Hormuz. Oman's stance on Hormuz is also presented inconsistently, with some Iranian reports of anger over alternative routes, while others mention dialogue for future administration. Unverified claims include over 50,000 missing in Venezuela (based on crowdsourced data) and reports of "Julani forces" gathering on the Lebanese border. Propaganda indicators are prevalent in both Iranian and Israeli state media, with Iran portraying the interim agreement as a "strategic victory" and Israel highlighting its military successes in Lebanon. Significant reporting gaps remain on the specific details of the pending Israel-Lebanon framework agreement and the exact scope and implications of the US-Iran "interim agreement," particularly concerning IAEA access to nuclear facilities.
